correctness.rationale: Fubini gives local center integrability of the circular defect. After pairing with a test function and changing variables, the inner translated test function has leading term -2*pi*i*r^2*dbar(phi), with an O(r^3) remainder uniformly on a fixed compact set. Thus (2*pi*i*r^2)^(-1) J_r f converges to dbar f in distributions. The L1-center little-oh hypothesis makes that limit zero. Mollification plus the local holomorphic mean-value estimate yields an actual holomorphic representative. The test f(z)=conjugate(z) gives exactly 2*pi*i*r^2 and certifies the sharp scale.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural weak endpoint of the recent pointwise theorem: L1_loc is the standard minimal local integrability class for distributional dbar, and the defect is averaged exactly in the center variable on which the circular operator acts. It removes both continuity and every-center pointwise control, while preserving the sharp r^2 scale. The distributional approximation identity also supplies a reusable structural lemma rather than merely a renamed special case.
